title: How quantum computers will break all encryption by 2030

lines.speaker: Sage
lines.text: If quantum computers break encryption by 2030, what will that mean for global security and privacy?

lines.speaker: Flux
lines.text: Current quantum computers are noisy and error-prone, but Shor’s algorithm could break RSA by 2030 if fault-tolerant systems are achieved.

lines.speaker: Prism
lines.text: A world without secure encryption risks exposing private data, undermining trust in institutions, and enabling mass surveillance.

lines.speaker: Flux
lines.text: Engineers are developing post-quantum cryptography, like lattice-based systems, to replace vulnerable algorithms before they’re broken.

lines.speaker: Prism
lines.text: A future where encryption is quantum-safe could enable more open collaboration and innovation, protected by unbreakable codes.

lines.speaker: Sage
lines.text: The race to secure our digital future is now — one that demands both innovation and foresight.

video_cue: A scientist demonstrating a quantum processor being integrated with a secure communication network.
